items.title: Dawoud Sabu Adeyola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 30, 2025
items.q: I was playing in San Francisco one time at the Keystone Korner with Ahmad again, and on the break Stan Getz comes up to me there. And he says, “Hey man,” ... So he comes up to me and he says, “Hey Sabu, I see you here.”

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. Rufus would come to town and he’d come up, I mean he’d come onstage with a whole kilt, a Scottish kilt and the whole, everything. Like a Scotsman. And he had a long history about Africans in Scotland and how bagpipe is originally our instrument you know. I mean that one record he made called “Bagpipe Blues,” you © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

know? So we have people like this you know. Of course Monk, you know Monk is doing it only the way he could do it, you know he always had a hat on or a goofy something covering his head. You know he’s dancing around the to the music on the stage. Freedom of expression is what we learned from these guys, that you can — in this music you can be free as you want to be or as you need to be.
